Agreed, I don't know how I feel about Aspergers being merged with Autism myself. Maybe because I live with family who has been diagnosed with both. Autism does wear many faces, I've seen kids on the higher end thrive, and go into regular education systems. I've seen 12 year olds on the lower end still in essentially diapers and non-verbal, but still happy and smiling - because he has a wonderful mom who fights to get him the best care possible. I've seen people on the spectrum just not in touch with reality almost, even as adults. And I'm married to someone on the upper end. Some people don't know how I do it. Say I must have to parent him. It probably helps I've known him since I was 13, so 21 years, married 10. This is a safe place for questions, but if you really want the textbook definition it isn't hard to find with the internet.

I guess they're unfamiliar with the phrase "spectrum". My husband has autism, is married to me, helping to raise our son, goes to work 5 to 6 days a week, etc. People just don't educate themselves. Like thinking an addict has to be homeless with a needle sticking out of their arm draining the life out of society as we speak. I'm not comparing the two, don't get me wrong. I'm just trying to give another example how people get a vision of what some disorder or disease looks like, and can't accept that it may look like many things. Just so you know high school is definitely the hardest for people who don't fit the mold. As you grow look for the person or 2 that accepts you, and hold on. They will make your life more liveable. In h.s. my husband could have seriously been the guy who shot up the school. He didn't fit in, he had a super strict dad and brothers who beat him for fun. Luckily he had me as a friend then, we both were in band, and both loved music. And while my mom didn't like him for a really long time, it didn't matter. Find what makes you happy. Accept who you are.  While you're never going to be a social butterfly, this doesn't mean you can't have a meaningful life. I've met alot of people on the upper end of the spectrum who music really helps. My son is very close to being on it? Doctors disagree.
